\caption{\textbf{Removing the gate duplicates subjects; dropping either branch or the per-head weights costs detail or coherence.} Four ablation prompts at 4096$\times$4096, seed 0; each prompt shows the full images and, below them, 1:1 crops of the outlined 512$\times$512 window (chosen automatically as the region with the most edge energy averaged over the six variants). No gate: the calibrated mix from the first step. $\pi=1$ and $\pi=0$: after the gate, the local or the global branch alone. Uniform $\pi(\sigma)$: one weight shared by all heads. Mean pooling: average-pooled instead of subsampled global keys. Without the gate the subject repeats across the canvas. $\pi=0$ crops show the coarse grid of the pooled branch, and mean pooling loses the layout. $\pi=1$ and uniform $\pi(\sigma)$ look close to SCA in these crops; their deficits show in the metrics.}
\label{fig:ablation_grid}
